t: Any expenditure made from funds provided in this title for procurement outside the United States of any commodity in bulk and in excess of $100,000 shall be reported to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives at least twice annually: Provided, That each such report shall state the reasons for which the President determined, pursuant to criteria set forth in section 604(a) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as amended, that foreign procurement will not result in adverse effects upon the economy of the United States or the industrial mobilization base which out-weigh the economic or other advantages to United States of less costly procurement outside the United States.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a mandatory report explaining the President's determination is a participatory procedure. But the report goes only to congressional appropriations committees, which are inside the federal government, and the determination is made by the President alone. No state, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted or given a right to comment, object, or sue.
fable.s: shall be reported to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives at least twice annually

qwen_block.w: This section requires the executive branch to report expenditures to congressional committees. Congress is considered part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. There is no consultation with states, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: Any expenditure made from funds provided in this title for procurement outside the United States of any commodity in bulk and in excess of $100,000 shall be reported to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives at least twice annually

opus.w: The only interaction this section requires is reporting to congressional Appropriations Committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The President makes the foreign-procurement determination alone, under existing criteria. The section calls for no consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body with anyone outside the government. Reading the reporting duty as participation fails because the process never crosses the federal boundary.
opus.s: shall be reported to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives at least twice annually

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the executive branch to report expenditures to congressional committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so reporting to them is not participation. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making the procurement decisions.
qwen_chat.s: Any expenditure made from funds provided in this title for procurement outside the United States of any commodity in bulk and in excess of $100,000 shall be reported to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives at least twice annually
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because the report explains a decision made by the President, it involves some form of oversight or consultation. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are "inside the federal government" and do not constitute participation. The section only mandates reporting *to* Congress, not consulting *with* them or any outside party before the decision is made.
